newsitem.title: USA: MGE spring wheat ends mixed, nearby March firms.
newsitem.headline: MGE spring wheat ends mixed, nearby March firms.

text.p: MGE spring wheat futures closed mixed, with nearby March wheat gaining on improved export prospects and on continued short-covering ahead of first notice day at the end of February.
"There seems to be the feeling that people want to be long the March going into first notice day and they don't want to be short the spreads," a trader said.
Traders said MGE contracts drew support from news that Mexico bought 50,000 tonnes of what was probably U.S. spring wheat for March/April delivery.
"It's clear that (spring wheat) business has been working its way down to Mexico and South America," a MGE broker said.
MGE spring wheat settled four cents per bushel lower to one cent higher, with March up one cent at $3.89-1/4.
Wheat markets were generally weaker on a lack of follow-through buying from Tuesday's rally and on bearish reaction to Wednesday's USDA supply and demand report.
USDA raised its estimate of 1996/97 wheat ending stocks to 474 million bushels from its January estimate of 469 million.
Wheat also weakened after East Asian grain trade sources downplayed speculation of improved U.S. wheat export prospects because of Canadian grain shipment problems.
Traders said the March/May spread continued to widen, trading out to 20 cents after having opened at 17 cents. ADM sold one million May bushels, which helped the spread widen.
